newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban issue new regulations for women.
newsitem.headline: Taleban issue new regulations for women.

text.p: The fundamentalist Islamic Taleban's religious police have issued new regulations in Kabul retricting Afghan women's access to aid and ordering them to avoid making noise with their shoes when they walk.

The religious police, formally known as the Department for Promoting Virtue and Preventing Vice, issued two memos last week; one to international aid agencies operating in Kabul, and one to hospitals.

"The regulations of our Islamic country are based on the non-employment of females in international or local offices, and issuing limits on women's rights to leave their houses is an Islamic obligation that must be observed by foreign and local institutions." says the memo sent to all international agencies.
The new regulations also formalise the laws that say that women are not allowed to work in any field apart from the medical sector.

"Women are not allowed to work in any field except the medical sector. Aid agencies need to gain permission from the Department for Promoting Virtue and Preventing Vice to employ or assist women," according to the regulations.
But even the women working in the medical sector have to observe certain regulations to conform to the Taleban's interpretation of Sharia, or Islamic law.
"No Afghan woman can take a senior or acting senior position in foreign-run hospitals.

"Women working in the medical sector should not sit in the seat next to the driver during transportation. No Afghan woman has the right to be transported in the same car as foreigners." say the regulations.
A large proportion of aid programmes are aimed at women, particularly Kabul's thousands of widows, many of whom have been driven to destitution by the Taleban ban on women working.
The regulations say that widows should only be assisted through their male relatives.
"We would appreciate it if assistance for both poor women and widows is channeled through their male relatives."

An aid worker in Kabul called the regulations impractical and said that if they were fully implemented they would increase the difficulties faced by the aid community in reaching the most vulnerable sections of Afghan society.

"They are impractical. If we implemented according to the regulations, we would have to stop all our programmes." said Ross Everson of the aid umbrella organisation Agency Coordination Body for Afghan Relief on Monday.
The regulations sent to hospitals ban women from visiting male patients in wards that contain non-family members and outlaw make-up, jewellery, and shoes with heels that make a noise when walking.
"It is forbidden for women to vist male patients in wards where unrelated males are hospitalised.

"Stylish dress and decoration of women in hospitals is forbidden. Women are duty-bound to behave with dignity, to walk calmly and refrain from hitting their shoes on the ground, which makes noises." say the regulations.

The Taleban's policies towards women have provoked protests from campaigners for women's rights in the west. The Taleban say that they are trying to implement a pure Islamic state and the regulations are neccessary to achieve that end.
